newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya eases sanctions on Burundi - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Kenya eases sanctions on Burundi - newspaper.

text.p: Kenya has lifted air transport sanctions against Burundi and eased a ban on fuel exports to the tiny Central African nation, the privately-owned Nation newspaper reported on Friday.

The paper quoted Assistant Foreign Affairs Minister, Sheldon Mushilwa, as saying that transport operators, including U.N. agencies, would no longer have to seek government clearance for flights to Burundi.
The minister, who was addressing parliament, said the government of President Daniel arap Moi would also allow war-torn and landlocked Burundi to buy limited amounts of fuel on humanitarian grounds.
Regional states imposed sanctions on Burundi shortly after military strongman Major Pierre Buyoya ousted civilian president Sylvestre Ntibantunganya in July last year.

Regional leaders demanded that Buyoya, a Tutsi heading a Tutsi military junta, open unconditional talks with Hutu rebels including the main group the National Council for the Defence of Democracy (CNDD).
But the sanctions were relaxed in April to encourage dialogue in the ethnically-divided tea and coffee-growing nation.
Buyoya has said formal talks with rebel and opposition groups would start this month in Arusha, northern Tanzania.
More than 150,000 people have been killed in Burundi in war pitting Buyoya's Tutsi-dominated army against the Hutus who are fighting for a greater political stake in their motherland.
Burundi has remained unstable after Tutsi soldiers murdered the country's first freely-elected president, Melchior Ndadaye, a Hutu.
